claims.text: Adding 0.5–1 at% boron to a phosphorus-containing Fe–Co–Cr–Ni–P high-entropy alloy will enhance short-range order.
Adding 0.5–1 at% boron will increase atomic packing density in the alloy.
The boron-induced structural changes will kinetically hinder crystallization during rapid quenching.
Adding 0.5–1 at% boron will improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Introducing boron during arc melting will ensure its uniform distribution before rapid quenching.
The beneficial effect is restricted to a boron concentration of 0.5–1 at%.
Excessive boron may cause phase separation or crystallite formation.
Small boron atoms induce enhanced short-range order and improved atomic packing density.
Boron has a small atomic radius.
Boron has a high negative heat of mixing in the proposed alloy system.
Boron’s size and heat-of-mixing characteristics promote stable, densely packed local atomic clusters.
The proposed local clusters act as kinetic barriers to nucleation and increase the barrier against crystallization.
Relative to the boron-free baseline, the boron-containing alloy will have a lower critical thickness for full amorphization.
Relative to the boron-free baseline, the boron-containing alloy will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature.
The proposed mechanism may require phosphorus and the other alloy constituents to permit formation of the dense clusters.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts improved glass-forming ability, but the stated outcome and falsification rule treat a reduction in critical casting thickness as improvement. Critical casting thickness is ordinarily a maximum fully glassy thickness, so improved glass-forming ability would correspond to an increase, not a reduction. If a different minimum coating-thickness metric is intended, it is not consistently defined.
